maps.title: Systems Design Corpus V2
maps.subtitle: A staged, model-assisted, source-grounded review draft.
maps.question: What are the major families inside systems design corpus v2, and what does each family claim about reality?
maps.summary: Staged draft assembled from 25 source chunks. Prompt: A comparison map of systems design patterns, constraints, failure modes, feedback/control, architecture, socio-technical systems, requirements, resilience, and complex-system tradeoffs.

groups.title: Systems Engineering And Lifecycle Architecture
groups.stance: Coordinates complex work through lifecycle models, requirements, architecture, verification, and validation.
groups.centralClaim: Complex systems need explicit lifecycle architecture so requirements, interfaces, and validation do not drift apart.
groups.whyItMatters: This family anchors the map because it supplies the integrative discipline: connecting stakeholders, models, requirements, and implementation across the system life cycle.

contributors.name: Systems engineering / SysML
contributors.reason: Systems engineering / SysML represents the source evidence for Systems Engineering And Lifecycle Architecture.

texts.title: Systems engineering and SysML source chunks

objections: Can become process-heavy or bureaucratic.
May understate political and organizational constraints.
Models can look complete while hiding implementation risk.

groups.title: Feedback And Control Systems
groups.stance: Designs systems around feedback loops, controllers, stability, and regulation of dynamic behavior.
groups.centralClaim: A system can be designed as something steered: sensors, controllers, feedback, and stability criteria keep behavior near intended goals.
groups.whyItMatters: This family adds a dynamic lens that v1 lacked: systems are not only built, they are regulated under changing conditions.

contributors.name: Control theory and feedback systems
contributors.reason: Control theory and feedback systems represents the source evidence for Feedback And Control Systems.

objections: Control models may oversimplify social or ambiguous goals.
Optimization can stabilize the wrong target.
Feedback delays can create oscillation or fragility.

groups.title: Failure, Resilience, And Risk Analysis
groups.stance: Starts from failure modes, criticality, reliability, mitigation, and resilience under stress.
groups.centralClaim: Good system design anticipates how components, interfaces, software, and organizations fail before failure appears in production.
groups.whyItMatters: This family is essential for review because it turns design from ideal operation into risk-aware operation.

contributors.name: FMEA and reliability engineering
contributors.reason: FMEA and reliability engineering represents the source evidence for Failure, Resilience, And Risk Analysis.

objections: Can reduce complex failures to checklist thinking.
Risk scores can create false precision.
Rare systemic failures may be missed by component-level analysis.

groups.title: Software Architecture And Computational Structure
groups.stance: Treats systems as modular computational structures of interfaces, data, algorithms, networks, and implementation constraints.
groups.centralClaim: Architecture decisions shape what can scale, what can change, what fails together, and what teams can reason about.
groups.whyItMatters: This family broadens systems design beyond generic engineering process into computational structure and software/system patterns.

contributors.name: Computer science and software architecture
contributors.reason: Computer science and software architecture represents the source evidence for Software Architecture And Computational Structure.

texts.title: Computer science and architecture source chunks

objections: Can become too abstract from operations.
Patterns may be copied without context.
Architecture diagrams can hide runtime behavior.

groups.title: Socio-Technical And Enterprise Systems
groups.stance: Frames systems as coupled technical, organizational, stakeholder, workflow, and enterprise structures.
groups.centralClaim: Many systems fail because the designed artifact and the human organization around it do not match.
groups.whyItMatters: This family corrects the narrow technical bias by making stakeholders, workflows, and enterprise architecture part of the design object.

contributors.name: Enterprise architecture and organizational systems
contributors.reason: Enterprise architecture and organizational systems represents the source evidence for Socio-Technical And Enterprise Systems.

texts.title: Zachman Framework and organizational systems sources

objections: Can become vague if every stakeholder concern is included.
Organizational evidence may be less formal than technical evidence.
Enterprise frameworks can over-document without improving decisions.

groups.title: Requirements And Design Process
groups.stance: Focuses on elicitation, analysis, negotiation, traceability, iteration, and problem definition.
groups.centralClaim: Requirements convert needs and constraints into design commitments that can be debated, built, verified, and revised.
groups.whyItMatters: This keeps the useful part of v1, but makes it one category rather than the entire map.

contributors.name: Requirements engineering
contributors.reason: Requirements engineering represents the source evidence for Requirements And Design Process.

texts.title: Requirements engineering and INCOSE/UML source chunks

objections: Requirements can freeze uncertainty too early.
Stakeholders may not know what they need.
Traceability can become paperwork if not tied to decisions.

groups.title: Constraints, Tradeoffs, And Scalability
groups.stance: Evaluates systems through cost, complexity, scalability, reliability, performance, maintainability, and assumptions.
groups.centralClaim: System design is mostly choosing constraints: improving one dimension often pressures another.
groups.whyItMatters: This family makes the system-comparison recipe explicit by foregrounding tradeoffs rather than only naming methods.

contributors.name: Scalability and data-system design
contributors.reason: Scalability and data-system design represents the source evidence for Constraints, Tradeoffs, And Scalability.

texts.title: Scalability, assumptions, and relational database source chunks

objections: Tradeoff language can become generic without concrete metrics.
Optimizing visible constraints may ignore hidden social costs.
Scalability concerns can dominate maintainability or safety.

groups.title: Complex And Adaptive System Behavior
groups.stance: Studies emergence, nonlinear behavior, load sharing, adaptation, and system-level behavior under stress.
groups.centralClaim: Some failures and behaviors only appear at the system level, after interactions compound beyond local components.
groups.whyItMatters: This family gives the map a nonlinear systems layer and prevents the packet from being only process and architecture.

contributors.name: Complex systems and load-sharing research
contributors.reason: Complex systems and load-sharing research represents the source evidence for Complex And Adaptive System Behavior.

objections: Can be too abstract for direct design decisions.
Emergent behavior is hard to verify before deployment.
Complexity explanations can become unfalsifiable if not tied to evidence.
